title_en: The Fall Solo Six-Pack: Sports Games, the Return of Discretionary Macro, & AI Coming for Y
title_zh: 秋季单人六连发（Solo Six-Pack）：孩子的比赛、主观宏观的回归，与 AI 逼近你的工作
subtitle_zh: Jeff 一人开六罐：青少年体育、Lakers 交易税盾与 AI 就业数据核查。
description: The Fall Solo Six-Pack: Sports Games, the Return of Discretionary Macro, & AI Coming for Y

turns.en: Welcome to The Derivative by RCM Alternatives. Send it. Hello there. Welcome back. You've found The Derivative brought to you by RCM Alternatives, where we're part of the sponsors, the CTA Expo here in town this week.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 RCM Alternatives 出品的 The Derivative。Send it。大家好，欢迎回来。这里是 RCM Alternatives 带给你的 The Derivative——本周在本城举办的 CTA Expo，我们也是赞助方之一。

turns.en: I've been at a bunch of kids golf events, regionals and sectionals, more on that in a quick second. So we didn't have a guest last week and mess it up this week.
turns.zh: 我这几天跑了一堆青少年高尔夫比赛，地区赛（regionals）和区段赛（sectionals），这个待会儿细说。上周我们没有嘉宾，这周干脆就把它搞砸一点。

turns.en: So you get me on a solo six pack here to start October. Hard to believe it's fall already. So where do we start? Wanted to start out with youth sports.
turns.zh: 所以十月的开场，就是我一个人给你们来一期“单人六连发”（solo six-pack）。真不敢相信已经入秋了。那从哪儿说起呢？我想先聊聊青少年体育。

turns.en: Six pack number one, open that beer. I was told by a kid less friend. Is that how I said that? A friend without kids the other day. I turned down an invite to something to head to a kid's softball game.
turns.zh: 六连发第一罐，开瓶吧。前几天有位没有孩子的朋友跟我说——我是这么说的吗？——反正就是位没孩子的朋友。我推掉了一个邀约，跑去看孩子的垒球赛。

turns.en: And he said basically, you know, you don't have to put them in all these travel teams. Your kids probably not going to go pro. That's only a good friend could tell you.
turns.zh: 他大概意思是：你知道的，没必要把孩子塞进这么多旅行队（travel team）。你家孩子大概率成不了职业球员——这话只有好朋友才会跟你说。

turns.en: And the kid will end up all right if you don't go to every game. So few things done pack here. One, I know my kids aren't going pro and I agree the prevalence of travel teams and lessons and training has gotten a little bit out of hand.
turns.zh: 而且就算你不是每场比赛都到场，孩子最后也会好好的。这罐里有几点想说：第一，我知道我家孩子成不了职业球员，我也同意，现在旅行队、私教课和训练泛滥得有点失控了。

turns.en: We talked about that on a pod with Scott Carl earlier this year. We'll put that in the show notes. It is ridiculous yet the team's called going pro, pro prospect, future stars, elite and such.
turns.zh: 今年早些时候我和 Scott Carl 做那期节目时聊过这个话题，我们会把那期放进节目备注里。这确实很离谱——可这些队伍的名字却叫“Going Pro”“Pro Prospect”“Future Stars”“Elite”之类的。

turns.en: It's like they're selling the berry flavored vape pens to preteens. Worst part is a lot of parents believe in this scam. I've talked to some who say that's their college savings plan scary.
turns.zh: 就像在卖给十二三岁的孩子浆果味的电子烟（vape pen）。最糟糕的是，很多家长真信这套骗局。我跟一些家长聊过，有人说这就是他们的大学储蓄计划——挺吓人的。

turns.en: But that was me. It's not our family, but we still do it. So why? It's nuance. High school, the high school picks people up the travel teams.
turns.zh: 但那说的不是我。这不是我们家的路子，可我们照样在做。为什么？因为这事有它的微妙之处：高中校队是从旅行队里挑人的。

turns.en: The kid wants to start, wants to play. That's extra lessons, extra works. So is it evil? Yes. Is it also maybe necessary to play sports in high school?
turns.zh: 孩子想首发、想上场，那就意味着额外的私教课、额外的训练。所以它是坏事吗？是。但它是不是也可能是在高中打上体育比赛的必要条件？

turns.en: Big Chicago school also yes. But to the other half of the friend's comment, you don't have to go to every one of your kids games. I like going to the games.
turns.zh: 在 Chicago 这种规模很大的高中，答案也是肯定的。不过回到我那位朋友说的另一半——“你没必要场场比赛都去”。可我就是喜欢去看比赛。

turns.en: I love going to the games. I'm a sports fan in general. You've heard me talk bears and cubs on here. And this is the ultimate sport to be a fan in, right?
turns.zh: 我特别爱去看比赛。我本来就是个体育迷，你们也听我在节目里聊过 Bears 和 Cubs。而孩子的比赛才是当球迷的终极体验，对吧？

turns.en: You get to be court side on the field, walking inside the ropes, whatever you want to call it. You get to hear what the coach is telling the player, get to see the player recover.
turns.zh: 你能坐在“场边第一排”、走在围栏绳以内，随你怎么叫它。你能听到教练跟球员说什么，能看到球员怎么调整回来。

turns.en: You get to see the training, get to see the mental side. But there's another bigger piece that this is finite, right? It's econ 101. There's only so much supply of your kids games.
turns.zh: 你能看到训练，看到心理层面的东西。但还有一个更重要的点：这是有限的，对吧？这就是经济学入门（Econ 101）——你孩子的比赛，供给就那么多。

turns.en: And then it's done. You can't make your kid 12 again and scalp some little league tickets and go watch them. Imagine if the bears were ceasing to exist as a team in two years.
turns.zh: 然后就没了。你没法让孩子回到 12 岁，再倒腾几张少棒联盟（Little League）的票去看他打球。想象一下，如果 Bears 这支球队两年后就不存在了。

turns.en: Maybe that's a bad example because they are looking at moving to Indiana. But imagine if, ignoring that, imagine if they were never going to be any more bears games.
turns.zh: 也许这个例子举得不好，因为他们确实在考虑搬到 Indiana。但先不管这个，想象一下以后再也不会有 Bears 的比赛了。

turns.en: The tickets would be astronomical, right? You'd drop everything and anything to go get to as many of those games as possible before they were gone.
turns.zh: 票价会贵到天上，对吧？你会放下一切，尽可能多地去现场看几场，趁它们还没消失。

turns.en: Which is what's happening in your kid's sports, right? There's only so many of them left. Which brings me to the sad start to this week. My son's a senior on the golf team.
turns.zh: 而孩子的体育比赛正是这么回事，对吧？剩下的场次就那么多了。这就说到本周这个有点伤感的开场：我儿子是高尔夫球队的毕业班（senior）队员。

turns.en: He made it through regionals, played in sectionals. He was one under through nine and in second place. Everyone was cheering, top ten make it through.
turns.zh: 他打过了地区赛（regionals），进了区段赛（sectionals）。前九洞他打出低于标准杆一杆，排在第二位，全场都在给他加油——前十名就能晋级。

turns.en: Then a double bogey, then a couple of pars, then a three put bogey, then another. Before I could get my heart rate back under 130, it was over.
turns.zh: 然后一个双柏忌（double bogey），接着几个帕（par），然后一个三推柏忌，再来一个。我的心率还没降回 130 以下，比赛就结束了。

turns.en: He missed going to state by a stroke. So why do I go? Because I'm a fan of my kid. I'm a fan of sports. And there's only so many games left.
turns.zh: 他以一杆之差无缘州赛（state）。那我为什么还要去现场？因为我是我孩子的球迷，我是体育的球迷，而且剩下的比赛就那么多了。

turns.en: And sadly, this week, no more games left for my senior. So if you're listening to this buddy, love you, proud of you, was fun watching you over the years.
turns.zh: 可惜这周之后，我家这位毕业班球员已经没有比赛可打了。所以小伙子，如果你听到这期节目：我爱你，我为你骄傲，这些年看你打球真的很开心。

turns.en: All right. That was a sad start. Let's get a little cheerier here, but thought that needed to be said. It's a weird thing for people to be like, why do you go to your kid's sports?
turns.zh: 好了，这个开场有点丧。我们让气氛欢快一点，但我觉得这话得说出来。别人问“你为什么老去看孩子的比赛”，这事儿本身就挺奇怪的。

turns.en: All right. Number two, open it up. I was at the CTA Expo yesterday. It was a conference that was around dozens and years ago, maybe a dozen years ago.
turns.zh: 好，第二罐，打开吧。昨天我去了 CTA Expo。这是个办了很多年的会议，可能得有十来年了。

turns.en: Took a few years off. Now it has come back. But it's fun to see a lot of the same characters, people I've known for 20 years or more. I did a panel.
turns.zh: 中间停办了几年，现在又回来了。能看到很多老面孔很有意思，都是些我认识 20 年甚至更久的人。我还参加了一场小组讨论。

turns.en: We titled it by Builder Partner, RCM Sponsored the Event. Basically, everyone said it's dumb to build in today's world. There's so many ways to outsource everything and anything.
turns.zh: 我们把那场讨论的主题定为“自建还是外包（build vs. buy）”，RCM 是这次活动的赞助方。基本上所有人都在说，在今天这个世界自己搞建设是愚蠢的，因为你几乎可以把任何环节都外包出去。

turns.en: Compliance to sales, to trade execution. I agree. That's why RCM is here. That's what we do for so many clients. But anyway, I typically don't like to prep for a panel.
turns.zh: 从合规、销售到交易执行都行。我同意。RCM 存在的意义就在这儿，这也是我们为很多客户做的事。总之，我一般不太喜欢为小组讨论开准备会。

turns.en: And actually, I sent an email to the fellow panelists last week, said there's a few things I hate more in life than panel prep calls, parentheses, Green Bay Packers, slow drivers in the left lane, people who take their socks off on the plane.
turns.zh: 其实上周我给同场的其他嘉宾发了封邮件，说这辈子我讨厌的事不多，但比“小组讨论准备会”更讨厌的有几样（括号）：Green Bay Packers、在左侧车道慢悠悠开车的司机、以及在飞机上脱袜子的人。

turns.en: So beg them that we didn't need to do a call. And I think the panels go better that way. It's not that you're not prepared. You can prepare on your own.
turns.zh: 所以我求他们别开这个会了。而且我觉得这样小组讨论反而效果更好。不是说你就不准备了——你可以自己准备。

turns.en: You can tell them some of the things you want to talk about. But without like this set questions, it comes out more natural, feels more like a podcast than a boring conference panel.
turns.zh: 你可以告诉他们你想聊哪些话题。但如果没有那些事先设定好的问题，聊出来会更自然，感觉更像一期播客，而不是一场无聊的会议小组讨论。

turns.en: And can generally can ask follow up questions for things I don't understand, things that interest me or I think would interest the audience.
turns.zh: 而且我一般还能追问：追那些我没听懂的、我自己感兴趣的，或者我觉得听众会感兴趣的东西。

turns.en: So anyway, conference, rest of the conference had a bunch of talk about liquid alts and futures and ETFs. There was one on AI, general consensus there was it's not there yet.
turns.zh: 总之，会议剩下的部分大量在谈流动性另类（liquid alts）、期货和 ETF。有一场是关于 AI 的，那边的普遍共识是“还没到时候”。

turns.en: I disagree. One of my main takeaways was that discretionary macro is kind of the new emerging strategy du jour. Conference is used to be filled with quants, talking quant things, dazzling with stories about machine learning and models and customer risk logic, all the rest.
turns.zh: 我不同意。我最主要的一个体会是，主观宏观（discretionary macro）差不多成了当下最时髦的新兴策略。以前这种会议满场都是量化的人，讲量化的东西，用机器学习、模型、定制化风险逻辑之类的故事让人眼花缭乱。

turns.en: But it just feels to me like all that is table stakes now, right? Like nobody's impressing you with how they use the computer, how they use data, how they use this, even with AI, it's like, okay, everyone's doing that.
turns.zh: 但在我看来，这些现在都只是入场门槛（table stakes），对吧？没人再会因为你怎么用电脑、怎么用数据、怎么用这些工具而对你刮目相看，即便是 AI 也一样——大家的反应就是：好吧，所有人都在做。

turns.en: So it used to separate you and make you different from the original discretionary futures trader guys used to make you feel more safe. But now it feels like we've come full circle, right?
turns.zh: 过去这些东西能让你脱颖而出，跟最早那批主观期货交易者区分开，也让人觉得更安全。但现在感觉我们绕了一整圈又回到原点，对吧？

turns.en: And any manager has instant access to sophisticated programming and testing and trade tech and risk metrics and all the rest that don't raise any eyebrows anymore.
turns.zh: 任何一个管理人现在都能立刻用上复杂的编程、回测、交易技术、风险指标等等，这些东西已经不会再让人多看你一眼了。

turns.en: And in fact, I think there's a bit of a feeling that anything, anyone comes up with in a systematic way has already been done. It's already out there.
turns.zh: 事实上，我觉得有那么一种感觉：任何人用系统化方式想出来的东西，早就有人做过了，市面上已经有了。

turns.en: You can get it at a bank risk premium desk. You can get it in a multi-strategy, you can get it at any one of these places, I think is some of this feeling.
turns.zh: 你在银行的风险溢价（risk premium）部门能买到，在多策略（multi-strategy）平台能买到，在这些地方随便哪一家都能买到——我觉得这就是那种情绪的一部分。

turns.en: And that one of the only original trade generators left is the human brain, right? So kind of this new bevy of discretionary guys who maybe think just like the old ones, but just different enough and fortunately in an unquantifiable way, that they become interesting portfolio pieces to people who've kind of done that, been there with all the systematic pieces.
turns.zh: 于是，剩下为数不多还能产生原创交易的东西，就是人脑，对吧？所以现在冒出了这么一批新的主观交易者，他们的思路也许跟老一辈差不多，但恰恰又足够不同——而且是幸运地以无法量化的方式不同——于是对那些已经在系统化那块“该做的都做过、该看的都看过”的人来说，他们成了很有意思的组合拼图。

turns.en: So it was interesting to see a few of these guys around the conference and seems like I'm seeing more and more of this might just be anecdotal evidence, but sure seems like a zag from 10 years ago when it felt like there'd be no discretionary guys left and girls and that would be all systematic.
turns.zh: 所以在会场上看到几个这样的人挺有意思的，而且我感觉这类人越来越多——这可能只是个人观察的轶事证据，但这确实像是跟十年前来了个反向转弯（zag）：那时候的感觉是以后不会再有主观交易者了，一切都会是系统化的。

turns.en: Maybe that is a preface for what happens to AI and the rest of the economy. All right, number three, that Lakers sale a few weeks ago, month and a half ago.
turns.zh: 也许这正是 AI 以及整个经济接下来会发生什么的一个序章。好，第三罐：几周前、大概一个半月前那笔 Lakers 的出售。

turns.en: So I'm a little late on this, I was trying to get a few guests to come on and talk about it. It's kind of interesting, a bunch of different pieces intersecting, hedge funds, float, tax all that.
turns.zh: 所以我聊这个有点晚了，我本来想请几位嘉宾上节目来谈。这事儿挺有意思，好几个不同的东西交织在一起：对冲基金、浮存金（float）、税务，等等。

turns.en: So wanted to just spend a little time on it. We'll start with the seller, Mark Walter. This is all over the news. You can Google it, go find out.
turns.zh: 所以就想花点时间说说。我们先从卖方 Mark Walter 开始。这事儿新闻上到处都是，你可以自己去 Google 一下。

turns.en: But when I first heard it, and people were getting mad that he was using insurance float to purchase assets, investing the insurance premiums of little old ladies, I was getting mad because that's what Warren Buffett has been doing and trumpeting for decades, right?
turns.zh: 但我第一次听说的时候，大家都在生气，气他用保险浮存金（insurance float）去买资产，拿老太太们交的保费去做投资——我生气的原因却是：这几十年来 Warren Buffett 不就一直这么干、还一直到处宣扬吗，对吧？

turns.en: He's considered the king of this. So I'm like, wait, why is this anyone different? Everyone's selling options, getting premium to invest elsewhere.
turns.zh: 他被视为这套打法的王者。所以我就想：等等，这有什么不一样的？所有人都在卖期权、收保费，然后拿去别处投资。

turns.en: And that's the whole game, right? That's what insurance is used for from an investment side. I get it. People didn't think they're buying sports teams with it and it seems, you know, nothing's charged, nothing is proven, but seems Mark Walters went a little crazy with it.
turns.zh: 这就是整个游戏的玩法，对吧？从投资角度看，保险就是拿来这么用的。我懂。只是大家没想到会有人拿它去买职业球队——而且你看，目前没有起诉、也没有定论，但看起来 Mark Walter 用这招用得有点疯了。

turns.en: Right, they're all getting that he was basically loaning monies to affiliates to buy all these teams or to pledge that capital to buy the teams.
turns.zh: 对吧，现在爆出来的都是：他基本上是把钱借给关联公司去买这些球队，或者用这笔资本去做质押来买球队。

turns.en: Right, he bought the Dodgers, Dodgers TV, the Lakers, Chelsea. So anyway, all that is rather interesting. And he was subpoenaed, all this stuff's coming out and he had to sell the Lakers.
turns.zh: 他买了 Dodgers、Dodgers 的转播网、Lakers，还有 Chelsea。总之这些都挺有意思。后来他收到了传票，这些东西全被扒出来，他就不得不卖掉 Lakers。

turns.en: The flip side of that, the interesting side, now the buyer, right? Sure, there was a poor seller. But conveniently, SpaceX stock gets unlocked August 6th and the new buyer comes in and purchased this August 12th.
turns.zh: 另一面才是有意思的那一面，也就是买家。当然，卖方那边挺惨的。但巧的是，SpaceX 的股票在 8 月 6 日解禁，新买家在 8 月 12 日进场买下了这支球队。

turns.en: So that was Iger and Kushner's brother. But did you know under the tax law, they can amortize the current value of those player contracts over the next 15 years?
turns.zh: 买家是 Iger 和 Kushner 的兄弟。但你知道吗，按税法，他们可以在接下来 15 年里对那些球员合同的现值进行摊销（amortize）？

turns.en: So I had Claude do some math on that and showed me, take it for what it's worth, but showed me that that's about $800 million a year in deductions.
turns.zh: 所以我让 Claude 帮我算了笔账，它算出来——你姑且一听——大约是每年 8 亿美元的税前扣除（deduction）。

turns.en: So for two guys sitting there, right, and they're big in the, I don't have the name of their firm in front of me, but Venture slash private equity that got into SpaceX, got into OpenAI, another company that SpaceX purchased.
turns.zh: 所以对这两个人来说，对吧——他们做的是，我手上没有他们公司的名字，但就是风投（VC）／私募股权（PE），投进了 SpaceX，也投进了 OpenAI，还有另一家被 SpaceX 收购的公司。

turns.en: So two guys sitting on a few billion dollars in unrealized gains that they could perhaps be unlocking soon. OpenAI has delayed their IPO, but for sure, one day happened.
turns.zh: 也就是说，两个人手握几十亿美元的未实现收益，而且很快可能就能解锁变现。OpenAI 把 IPO 推迟了，但总有一天肯定会上市。

turns.en: So it's going to save them a ton of tax, right? They get that $800 million deduction, they've got all that SpaceX AI money coming in. So, and then they get to own the Lakers after the fact.
turns.zh: 所以这会给他们省下一大笔税，对吧？他们拿到那 8 亿美元的扣除额，又有 SpaceX、AI 那一大堆钱要进来。然后顺带还拥有了 Lakers。

turns.en: Steve Bomber, who's himself in trouble for skirting some of the rules, did all this when he bought the Clippers. Again, some cloud research there shows about 600 million or so of losses on those tax returns, despite the value of the franchise going up.
turns.zh: Steve Ballmer 当年买 Clippers 的时候就是这么干的，而他自己也因为绕过某些规则而惹上了麻烦。同样，用 Claude 做的一些研究显示，尽管这家俱乐部的价值一直在涨，但他报税单上却有大约 6 亿美元的亏损。

turns.en: So cool story to me, they weren't just buying a scarce trophy asset, they're buying a deduction and tax savings also. And right, what's that worth to someone with that money gains?
turns.zh: 所以这个故事在我看来很有意思：他们买的不只是一个稀缺的奖杯资产（trophy asset），同时还买到了一个扣除额和一笔节税。对吧，对一个有那么多收益的人来说，这值多少钱？

turns.en: And then also makes me think just right, if half the brainpower and money and time spent all the time on saving money on taxes went into curing cancer or doing something more useful, we'd have licked that many, many years ago, probably without AI.
turns.zh: 这也让我想到：如果把大家一直花在省税上的脑力、金钱和时间拿一半出来去攻克癌症，或者做点更有用的事，我们可能很多很多年前就把它解决了，而且大概还用不着 AI。

turns.en: All right, number four, speaking of billionaires, I was lucky enough to join some friends for a Utah golf trip, playing at some rather exclusive resorts, not to brag, but it was fun, came across the story of Promontory out there.
turns.zh: 好，第四罐。说到亿万富翁——我有幸跟几个朋友去 Utah 打了一趟高尔夫，在几家相当高端私密的度假村打了球（不是炫耀，但确实很好玩），其间听说了 Promontory 这个地方的故事。

turns.en: We played that long story short, the developer who was the founder of Pivotal, which has been big in real estate in the Southwest and up into Utah, as I read the story and did some research, they borrowed about 350 million or so to do the project.
turns.zh: 我们就在那儿打的球。长话短说，那个开发商是 Pivotal 的创始人，这家公司在美国西南部和 Utah 一带的房地产领域做得很大。我看故事、做了一些研究后发现，他们为这个项目借了大约 3.5 亿美元。

turns.en: Then GFC came 2008, 2009, had to default, lots weren't selling all the rest, went back and forth between lean holders, debtors, nobody could agree what to do with it.
turns.zh: 然后全球金融危机（GFC）来了，2008、2009 年，他们不得不违约，地块卖不出去，等等。之后在抵押权人（lien holders）和债务人之间来回折腾，谁也谈不拢该怎么处理。

turns.en: So it went to auction. Nobody showed up at the auction, except for the Pivotal owner and Pivotal bought it back for just $30 million in 09 after defaulting on 300 million or so, not a bad deal.
turns.zh: 于是项目被拿去拍卖。拍卖会上没人出现，除了 Pivotal 的老板自己——Pivotal 在 09 年只花了 3,000 万美元就把它买了回来，而之前违约的债务是 3 亿美元左右。这买卖不亏。

turns.en: Especially when we were talking about it over dinner out there, that it reportedly did over 600 million in home and lot sales in 25. So it's interesting, as that story was, there's lots of deals to be had at the bottom in 2009.
turns.zh: 尤其是我们在当地吃晚饭时聊到，据说它在 25 年的住宅和地块销售额超过了 6 亿美元。所以这个故事有意思的地方在于：2009 年的底部，遍地都是这种好交易。

turns.en: A rather famous Chicago prop firm guy bought up a lot of real estate in that period with some of the gains from his convex trades. Speaking of right, why do you want to have convex and have money when the markets are selling off so you can buy stuff at discounts like this?
turns.zh: 有一位挺出名的 Chicago 自营交易公司（prop firm）的人，就在那段时间用自己凸性（convexity）交易赚来的钱买下了大量房地产。说到这个，对吧——你为什么希望自己的持仓有凸性、在市场大跌时手里有钱？就是为了能像这样打折买东西。

turns.en: But it's interesting and all that was the a bit of a different take I walked away with. You know, as you're walking these courses or in the carts on these courses and you look around, there's just 10 million, 20 million, 30 million dollar home one after the other, landing every fairway.
turns.zh: 但真正让我带着走的，是一个有点不一样的视角。你在这些球场里走路或者坐球车，环顾四周，就看到一栋接一栋 1,000 万、2,000 万、3,000 万美元的房子，沿着每一条球道排开。

turns.en: And so my brain goes, so how does that 10 million dollar second home bonanza end? Right, like New York City, others are trying to tax those second home, second home tax.
turns.zh: 于是我脑子里就在想：这波 1,000 万美元第二住宅的狂欢会怎么收场？对吧，比如 New York City 和其他一些地方已经在想办法对第二住宅征税了——“第二住宅税”。

turns.en: I'm an alternatives guy, right? So I'm always thinking this is a bubble. I'm looking up at these houses. They're mostly empty and saying, you know, just what happens here?
turns.zh: 我是做另类投资（alternatives）的，对吧？所以我总会觉得这是个泡沫。我抬头看着这些房子，大多是空的，心里就在想：这儿到底会发生什么？

turns.en: I'm thinking the money's too easy when I see all that where to come from and where is it going next? But surprisingly to myself, then I said, well, hold on, maybe this is an opportunity.
turns.zh: 看到这一切，我觉得钱来得太容易了——这些钱从哪儿来，接下来又要去哪儿？但让我自己都意外的是，我接着又想：等等，也许这是个机会。

turns.en: Right, maybe this is the tip of the iceberg and we see more and more of this. This place out there is unbelievable. They've got multiple golf courses, movie theaters, bowling alleys, beach club, biking, hiking, golfing, skiing, hot air balloons.
turns.zh: 对吧，也许这只是冰山一角，以后我们会看到越来越多这样的地方。那边这个社区简直难以置信：好几个高尔夫球场、电影院、保龄球馆、沙滩俱乐部，还有骑行、徒步、高尔夫、滑雪、热气球。

turns.en: Hunting, fishing, gyms, basically whatever you can think of. I was talking with one guy is like, we're trying to get a reservoir and get a big lake where they can have like actual water skiing and boats and whatnot.
turns.zh: 打猎、钓鱼、健身房，基本上你能想到的都有。我跟一个人聊天，他说：我们正在争取建一个水库、造一个大湖，这样就能搞真正的水上滑水、开船之类的。

turns.en: So made me think the rest is a movement. Maybe I'm just late to realizing and are talking about it. But do we see more of these kind of mini cities where the elite of the elite don't need to rub elbows with the rest of us and just have their 10, 20, 30 million dollar home?
turns.zh: 所以这让我觉得，这其实是一场运动（movement）。也许只是我意识到、开始谈论它太晚了。但我们是不是会看到越来越多这样的“迷你城市”——精英中的精英不必再和我们这些人打交道，就守着自己那栋 1,000 万、2,000 万、3,000 万美元的房子？

turns.en: Probably by the time this all happens be 50, 70, 100 million dollar home and they don't need to go out. You know, I think they'll miss the dive bar, that new restaurant in town, a bear's game, too much fun stuff outside of a planned community.
turns.zh: 等这一切真的成型的时候，房子大概已经是 5,000 万、7,000 万、1 亿美元的了，而他们根本不需要出门。不过我觉得他们会错过一些东西：街边的小酒馆、城里新开的那家餐厅、一场 Bears 的比赛——规划社区之外有太多好玩的东西了。

turns.en: But also think, you know, in this winter, take all AI economy and trillion dollar IPOs and widening wealth gap and all that sure makes sense that you don't just live anymore in the big house on tons of property in whatever town that you basically just go live amongst your centimillionaire peers, fishing, golfing, going for hot air balloon ride, which then makes me think the caddies, the fish guides, the plumbers and roofers for those homes.
turns.zh: 但换个角度想：在这个赢者通吃（winner-take-all）的 AI 经济里，有万亿美元级别的 IPO、财富差距不断拉大，那么“不再只是住在某个小镇上一栋占地巨大的大房子里”，而是直接搬去和你的亿级富豪（centimillionaire）同类住在一起——钓鱼、打高尔夫、坐热气球——这就很说得通了。而这又让我想到那些人：球童、钓鱼向导，以及给这些房子干活的水管工和屋顶工。

turns.en: That's probably the AI proof job market of the future in the walled resorts of the AI ballers. Number five, number five already. All right, number five.
turns.zh: 这大概就是未来那个“AI 打不倒”的就业市场——就藏在 AI 大佬们那些带围墙的度假村里。第五罐，已经第五罐了。好，第五罐。

turns.zh: 好，这封来自 New Jersey 的 Mark T。说到 New Jersey，有没有人在 ESPN 上看了 Mount Carmel 那场橄榄球赛？大概是九月初吧。

turns.zh: 他们是我们 Chicago 这边一支强得吓人的橄榄球队。而他们对阵的正是一支 New Jersey 的球队——说到 Mark T 嘛。Chicago 这边一度落后 30 分，最后逆转赢了。

turns.en: But I was watching with some guys and told them New Jersey guys are tough. I remember hitting some of them on the football field in college in New York was like hitting a brick wall.
turns.zh: 我当时跟几个朋友一起看，我就跟他们说 New Jersey 的人很硬。我记得大学时在 New York 的橄榄球场上撞上过几个 New Jersey 来的球员，那感觉就像撞上一堵砖墙。

turns.en: So Mark T, I'm assuming you're one of these tough guys. Anyway, Mark T says, why don't you have more of the RCM team on the podcast? Hmm. Good question. I'm not sure if that's a shot at me, but good question. Answer is they're busy. Maybe they're shy. We didn't think of it.
turns.zh: 所以 Mark T，我猜你就是那种硬汉之一。总之，Mark T 问：为什么你们不让更多 RCM 团队的同事上节目？嗯，好问题。我不确定这是不是在暗讽我，但确实是个好问题。答案是：他们很忙。也许他们害羞。也许我们根本没想到这件事。

turns.en: Somewhere in between all those is the answer. We did have Bobby Schwartz on as a guest earlier this year. So check that one out. But maybe instead of one of these solo six packs next time, we do a little mid-year review, which strategies are doing well, which are struggling.
turns.zh: 真实答案大概就在这几个之间。今年早些时候我们确实请了 Bobby Schwartz 来当嘉宾，大家可以去听那一期。不过也许下次不做这种“单人六连发”，我们做一期年中小结：哪些策略表现好，哪些在挣扎。

turns.en: I kind of like it. Might see in 27, bring on like John Cummings or someone who's in on all the different strategies. All right, next had one asking about why there isn't a morning style box for different managed futures strategies. I'm not sure where he's talking about on our website. Or he said it's long term, it's short term, it holds these markets.
turns.zh: 我挺喜欢这个主意的。也许到 27 年，我们会请 John Cummings 或者其他能覆盖所有不同策略的人来。好，下一位问的是：为什么没有一个针对各类管理期货（managed futures）策略的晨星风格箱（Morningstar style box）。我不确定他说的是我们网站上的哪个地方。他说这个是长期、那个是短期、它持有这些市场，

turns.en: He says it's very confusing without getting into all the strategies, how to just quickly view them. So I like it. We do do something like that on the database side of the RCM website. Maybe this is an AI project we can tackle. But what we mostly do, and this is probably why is coming for us, because this is what we've done for the last 20 years. But right, our team knows 20 to 30 managers really, really, really well, like which trades they did last and which markets they dropped
turns.zh: 他说这非常令人困惑，能不能在不深入每一种策略的情况下，快速地把它们看清楚。我喜欢这个问题。我们在 RCM 网站的数据库那块确实做了类似的东西，也许这是个我们可以用 AI 来解决的项目。但我们主要做的事情——这也可能就是 AI 要来抢我们饭碗的原因，因为这正是我们过去 20 年一直在做的——是：我们团队对 20 到 30 家管理人了解得非常、非常、非常透，比如他们上一笔做了什么交易、哪些市场他们

turns.en: four years ago, which are their new markets and really well, the next hundred or so we know well. But really what we do is meet and talk with the investors detail all those specifics, answer those questions. And then of course, put you in touch with the manager. I can see this question is like, Hey, before I get to that point, how do I just quickly sort these? So good question. Don't have an easy answer for you. Try and figure that one out. And then one from Todd
turns.zh: 四年前就已经放弃了、哪些是他们新进入的市场；再往外的下一百来家，我们也了解得不错。但我们真正做的，是跟投资人见面、聊，把所有这些细节讲清楚、回答这些问题，然后当然，把你和管理人对接上。我能理解这个问题的意思其实是：嘿，在我走到那一步之前，我怎么才能快速地把它们分个类？所以，好问题。我没有简单的答案给你，我们会想办法搞清楚。然后是 Todd

turns.en: W here, who says, we haven't had any talk about tail hedging in a while. You're right, Todd. Let's fix that. We can solve that with an upcoming guest. But it brings up the complacency in this market. Like that even shocked me. I went back and looked. Yeah. So when even the podcast has probably had the most tail hedging, guests and content of any podcast out there, when even we haven't done one in a while,
turns.zh: W 的来信，他说：你们已经有一阵子没聊尾部对冲（tail hedging）了。你说得对，Todd，我们来解决这个问题，可以靠接下来的一位嘉宾来解决。但这也反映出这个市场的自满情绪——这一点连我自己都吓了一跳，我回去查了一下，确实是这样。要知道，The Derivative 可能是所有播客里请过最多尾部对冲嘉宾、做过最多相关内容的节目，而连我们都有一阵子没做过这个话题了，

turns.en: how complacent is this market and ready for a sell off? It seems a good tail. It's like a reverse magazine indicator of has the derivative had a tail hedge guy on in a while.
turns.zh: 那这个市场得有多自满、对一轮抛售准备得有多不充分？这似乎是个不错的尾部信号——就像一个反向的“杂志封面指标”：The Derivative 有多久没请尾部对冲的人上节目了。
